plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, fragrant, bowl-shaped double or single blooms atop sturdy stems with glossy, deeply lobed green foliage. A beloved cottage garden staple that can live for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Central and East Asia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live over 100 years, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on nectar, though they are not required for blooming.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: A vigorous, arching wild shrub with five-petaled, softly scented flowers followed by bright red rose hips in autumn. Common in hedgerows and woodland edges.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (late May to July)
plants.location: Hedgerows and scrublands across Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: During World War II, rose hips from dog roses were collected in Britain to make vitamin C-rich syrup because citrus fruits were scarce.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A striking tropical to subtropical tree that bursts into clouds of lavender-blue trumpet-shaped flowers, often before its fern-like leaves fully emerge. Blooms carpet streets and pavements in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Mexico, Southern California, Florida, the Mediterranean, and parts of Africa and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas earned it the nickname 'Jacaranda City', and in parts of Australia a falling bloom is said to bring good luck on exams.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.description: A rugged Australian evergreen tree with serrated leathery leaves and tall, cylindrical flower spikes made up of hundreds of tiny flowers that attract honeyeaters and native bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to winter in the Southern Hemisphere (roughly February to August, with strong flowering around May)
plants.location: Coastal and sandy soils of eastern Australia, from Queensland to Victoria and Tasmania
plants.funFact: Banksia seed cones are adapted to fire and often open to release seeds only after bushfires, which helps regeneration.
